readings: For each invoice, together with its customer's country, compute the average `UnitPrice` of its invoice lines. Take the overall average of these invoice averages, and for each invoice compute its deviation (invoice average minus overall average). Then, for each country, average these deviations over its invoices. For each invoice, show the invoice id, country, average unit price, deviation from the overall average, and that deviation minus its country's average deviation. Sort by this last value from highest to lowest (blanks last) and return the top 10, including every invoice tied with the 10th one. Don't round.
queries:
WITH invoice_averages AS (
    SELECT i.InvoiceId, c.Country, AVG(il.UnitPrice) AS average_unit_price
    FROM Invoice AS i
    JOIN Customer AS c ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId
    LEFT JOIN InvoiceLine AS il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId
    GROUP BY i.InvoiceId, c.Country
),
deviations AS (
    SELECT InvoiceId, Country, average_unit_price,
           average_unit_price - AVG(average_unit_price) OVER () AS deviation
    FROM invoice_averages
),
results AS (
    SELECT InvoiceId, Country, average_unit_price, deviation,
           deviation - AVG(deviation) OVER (PARTITION BY Country) AS difference
    FROM deviations
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT *,
           RANK() OVER (ORDER BY difference IS NULL, difference DESC) AS position
    FROM results
)
SELECT InvoiceId, Country, average_unit_price, deviation, difference
FROM ranked
WHERE position <= 10
ORDER BY difference IS NULL, difference DESC
